title: The Retreat of Owlman
causes: The aggressive expansion of the Vedda horse-tamers across the Ganges Plain
The clearing of the deep deciduous forests by early charcoal-burners
outcomes: The withdrawal of the three-hundred-and-sixty-degree forest sentinel deeper into the southern Western Ghats
The founding of the hidden tree-temples by Jharwa-Vanara outlier populations to shelter Owlman's quiet spirit
A permanent cultural shift where human-Vanara hybrid descendants became reclusive guardians of the southern canopy
summary: As the horse-taming Vedda clans clear the central forests for pasture, the ancient avian guardian Owlman retreats deep into the Western Ghats. A reclusive group of Jharwa-Vanara outliers construct the first hidden tree-temples to protect his fading presence.
sources: The Stone Scrolls of Dwarka Fortress
